sets.title: Units produced by a footwear company across plants: pie chart shares and table. Total = 20,000 units. Shares in the pie are percentages of the total.

questions.questionText: In Tiruppur, how many units produced are there that do NOT form part of the number of defective units? (Answer as the remaining count.)
questions.explanation: Total in Tiruppur = 4,600; number of defective units = 276. Remaining = 4,324.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the table part from the pie amount.

questions.questionText: How many units produced are there in Erode?
questions.explanation: 9% of 20,000 = 1,800 units. So the required answer is 1,800 units.

questions.questionText: In which plant is the number of defective units the highest?
questions.explanation: Computed values: Coimbatore 320, Trichy 300, Salem 156, Madurai 44, Erode 108, Tiruppur 276. Highest is Coimbatore.
questions.shortcut: Compute every row; the largest share need not give the largest answer.

questions.questionText: By how much does the number of defective units in Trichy exceed that in Tiruppur?
questions.explanation: Trichy: 300; Tiruppur: 276. Difference = 24 units.

questions.questionText: By how much does the number of defective units in Salem differ (in absolute terms) from the average number of defective units per row? (Round to one decimal place if needed.)
questions.explanation: Total = 1,204; average over 6 rows = 200.67. Salem = 156. Difference = 44.7 units.

questions.questionText: What is the number of women voters in Central?
questions.explanation: Central: share 28% of 2,00,000 = 56,000 (voters). Using the table value gives 33,600 voters.
questions.shortcut: Find the pie amount first, then apply the table value.

questions.questionText: What is the ratio of the number of women voters in West to that in North, in simplest form?
What is the combined number of women voters in North and Central?
questions.explanation: North: 6,600; Central: 33,600. Sum = 40,200 voters.

questions.questionText: In which constituency is the number of women voters the highest?
questions.explanation: Computed values: North 6,600, South 12,000, East 23,100, West 22,800, Central 33,600, Rural 16,000. Highest is Central.
questions.shortcut: Compute every row; the largest share need not give the largest answer.

questions.questionText: By how much does the number of women voters in East differ (in absolute terms) from the average number of women voters per row? (Round to one decimal place if needed.)
questions.explanation: Total = 1,14,100; average over 6 rows = 19,016.67. East = 23,100. Difference = 4,083.3 voters.

questions.questionText: What is the number of candidates who passed in Chennai?
questions.explanation: Chennai: share 18% of 20,000 = 3,600 (candidates). Using the table value gives 1,260 candidates.
questions.shortcut: Find the pie amount first, then apply the table value.

questions.questionText: How many candidates are there in Chennai?
questions.explanation: 18% of 20,000 = 3,600 candidates. So the required answer is 3,600 candidates.

questions.questionText: In which centre is the number of candidates who passed the highest?
questions.explanation: Computed values: Chennai 1,260, Coimbatore 960, Madurai 1,540, Trichy 2,280, Salem 320, Vellore 1,800. Highest is Trichy.
questions.shortcut: Compute every row; the largest share need not give the largest answer.

questions.questionText: The number of candidates who passed across all rows is what percent of the total candidates? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Sum over all rows = 8,160. Percentage = 8,160/20,000 x 100 = 40.8%.
questions.shortcut: Add the row values; a simple average of the column is wrong because weights differ.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the total number of candidates who passed (across all rows) is contributed by Coimbatore and Vellore together? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: (960 + 1,800) / 8,160 x 100 = 33.8%. So the required answer is 33.8%.

questions.questionText: How many students are there in Law?
questions.explanation: 6% of 40,000 = 2,400 students. So the required answer is 2,400 students.

questions.questionText: In which faculty is the number of girls the highest?
questions.explanation: Computed values: Engineering 3,480, Arts 2,400, Science 960, Law 720, Management 3,600, Medicine 4,000. Highest is Medicine.
questions.shortcut: Compute every row; the largest share need not give the largest answer.

questions.questionText: What is the combined number of girls in Science and Engineering?
questions.explanation: Science: 960; Engineering: 3,480. Sum = 4,440 girls.

questions.questionText: By how much does the number of girls in Medicine exceed that in Management?
questions.explanation: Medicine: 4,000; Management: 3,600. Difference = 400 girls.

questions.questionText: By how much does the number of girls in Management differ (in absolute terms) from the average number of girls per row? (Round to one decimal place if needed.)
questions.explanation: Total = 15,160; average over 6 rows = 2,526.67. Management = 3,600. Difference = 1,073.3 girls.

questions.questionText: What is the number of female employees in HR?

questions.questionText: In which department is the number of female employees the highest?

questions.questionText: What is the ratio of the number of female employees in HR to that in Testing, in simplest form?
questions.explanation: HR: 680; Testing: 325. Ratio = 136:65. So the required answer is 136:65.

questions.questionText: What is the combined number of female employees in Finance and HR?
questions.explanation: Finance: 560; HR: 680. Sum = 1,240 female employees.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the total number of female employees (across all rows) is contributed by Finance and Support together? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: (560 + 400) / 3,665 x 100 = 26.2%. So the required answer is 26.2%.

questions.questionText: In which gate is the number of children the highest?

By how much does the number of children in Gate 2 exceed that in Gate 4?

questions.questionText: What is the combined number of children in Gate 3 and Gate 1?
questions.explanation: Gate 3: 3,600; Gate 1: 3,200. Sum = 6,800 children.

questions.questionText: The number of children in Gate 2 is what percent more than that in Gate 4? (Round to one decimal place.)
In which brand is the total sales revenue (Rs thousand) the highest?

questions.explanation: Realme: share 17% of 5,000 = 850 (phones sold). Using the table value gives Rs 12,750 thousand.

questions.questionText: What is the combined total sales revenue (Rs thousand) in Realme and Samsung?
questions.explanation: Realme: 12,750; Samsung: 11,000. Sum = Rs 23,750 thousand.

questions.questionText: By how much does the total sales revenue (Rs thousand) in Redmi exceed that in Realme?
questions.explanation: Redmi: 27,000; Realme: 12,750. Difference = Rs 14,250 thousand.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the total total sales revenue (Rs thousand) (across all rows) is contributed by Oppo and Vivo together? (Round to one decimal place.)
In which crop is the total production (quintals) the highest?
questions.explanation: Computed values: Paddy 14,50,000, Sugarcane 7,50,000, Cotton 5,60,000, Groundnut 4,80,000, Maize 3,50,000, Banana 6,90,000. Highest is Paddy.
questions.shortcut: Compute every row; the largest share need not give the largest answer.

questions.questionText: By how much does the total production (quintals) in Paddy exceed that in Banana?
questions.explanation: Paddy: 14,50,000; Banana: 6,90,000. Difference = 7,60,000 quintals.

questions.questionText: Taking all rows together, what is the overall average of the last column of the data (that is, the sum of the total production (quintals) over all rows divided by the total hectares cultivated)? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total = 42,80,000. Overall average = 42,80,000/50,000 = 85.6 quintals.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average, not a simple average of the table column.

questions.questionText: What is the combined total production (quintals) in Sugarcane and Groundnut?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane: 7,50,000; Groundnut: 4,80,000. Sum = 12,30,000 quintals.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the total total production (quintals) (across all rows) is contributed by Cotton? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Cotton = 5,60,000; total over all rows = 42,80,000. Share = 13.1%.

questions.questionText: The monthly payroll (Rs thousand) in Stores is what percent more than that in Quality? (Round to one decimal place.)
